newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Iceland expects to seal aluminium deal by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: Iceland expects to seal aluminium deal by yr-end.

text.p: Iceland's energy marketing body said on Monday that it expected to finalise a contract for a new aluminium smelter with the U.S.'s Columbia Ventures Corp by the end of the year.

Gardar Ingvarsson, managing director of the Icelandic Energy Marketing Agency, said construction would start early next year with initial production of 60,000 tonnes a year scheduled to begin in May 1998.
"We are working on the contract and trying to finalise it as soon as possible," Ingvarsson told Reuters by telephone from Reykjavik.
"We have not yet finalised it but we hope to finalise it by the end of this year and hope to start construction early next year.
"Negotiations are progressing very well and there have been no snags but it takes time."
Ingvarsson said initial production of 60,000 tonnes would be expanded over time.
Columbia Ventures Corp, run by lawyer Kenneth Peterson, was initially looking at locating a smelter it had bought in Germany in either Iceland or Venezuela.
The smelter will be the second in Iceland.
The current smelter, run by Swiss-based Alusuisse-Lonza Holdings AG, is currently undergoing a two-year, $200 million expansion project to boost capacity to 160,000 tonnes a year from 100,000 tonnes.
